@graph.name: Case Palletizer
@graph.description: A case palletizer is an automated system that receives sealed shipping cases from the case packer and stacks them onto pallets in a programmed pattern, ready for stretch wrapping and shipping. TRF Industrial Automation builds case palletizers on TRFCobot, TRFCompact and TRFSpeed, or as a custom palletizer, and the right model is defined by your line setup and speed.

mainEntity.name: Who Makes Robotic Case Palletizers With Local Support in the US?

acceptedAnswer.text: TRF Industrial Automation designs, builds and installs robotic case palletizers for manufacturers in the United States, on TRFCobot, TRFCompact, TRFSpeed or as a custom palletizer. TRF also supplies the case packing and conveying around the palletizer, and supports TRF equipment after startup through Parts and Service, with technical support, spare parts and preventive maintenance.

mainEntity.name: How Many Cases per Minute Can a Robotic Palletizer Handle?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the platform. TRFCobot covers about 1 to 10 cases per minute, TRFCompact about 5 to 15 and TRFSpeed about 10 to 35. These are typical ranges for commercial screening: TRF confirms the final rate for your cases, end-of-arm tool, pallet pattern and reach, and adds the time the cell spends on pallet exchange and changeovers.

mainEntity.name: Can One Case Palletizer Handle Different Case Sizes and Pallet Patterns?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, within the validated application. Each case size and pallet pattern is stored as a recipe, so the same palletizer can serve several SKUs, and the operator selects the pattern when the line changes over. The limits are the size range of the end-of-arm tool, the reach of the robot and how many pallet positions the layout allows.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Typical Payback Period for a Robotic Palletizer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Payback depends on the labor hours the palletizer replaces, shifts per day, local labor cost and the installed cost of the system. The palletizing ROI calculator applies this method to your location, your shifts and the people who palletize by hand today. On a case line, also note the value of a palletizer that keeps pace with the case packer instead of capping its output.

mainEntity.name: Can a Case Palletizer Operate Below Freezing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, with TRFSubzero, the TRF palletizer for areas below 32°F, built for frozen food, ice cream and other below-freezing areas. Rate and load are validated per application with your cases. The Custom Foods case study shows a TRF palletizing project below freezing.

mainEntity.name: What Is Slip Sheet Palletizing and When Is It Needed?

acceptedAnswer.text: A slip sheet is a sheet placed on the pallet deck or between layers. It adds friction between smooth case surfaces, spreads the load of the layers above and helps column patterns stay square. It is needed when the case surface, the pattern or the customer's rules call for it. On TRFSpeed, slip sheet handling is part of the integration scope.

mainEntity.name: How Much Does a Case Palletizer Cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cost depends on the platform, peak rate, case weight, tooling, pallet positions, pallet handling and conveyor integration. As a reference, list prices are US$ 120,000 for the TRFCobot Dual, US$ 180,000 for the TRFCompact Dual and US$ 350,000 for the TRFSpeed 100, EX Works Lenexa, Kansas, installation not included. The robotic palletizer cost page explains each cost factor.
